intervals.label: set-up of the 1 kg SSG detector
intervals.note: Start: year of the review that says the collaboration 'is setting up' the detector. End: the first data taking reported, in 2002 (arXiv:astro-ph/0404311, Sec. 3). Neither date is published as such.
intervals.quote: the ORPHEUS collaboration is setting up a 1kg SSG detector

intervals.label: operation of the 0.45 kg SSG detector
intervals.note: Start: first data taking in 2002; the 2004 abstract says the detector 'is operating'; the February 2005 review lists it as 'in operation'. The end is the last evidence of operation, not a shutdown date.
intervals.quote: The ORPHEUS dark matter detector is operating at our underground laboratory in Bern (70 m.w.e.).

intervals.label: run of two months at 170 mK
intervals.note: Year precision; the paper gives no start month.
intervals.quote: We were able to take data continuously during two months in 2002 at a temperature of 170 mK

intervals.label: run of three weeks at 115 mK
intervals.note: Year precision; the paper gives no start month. This run used an upgraded acquisition system.
intervals.quote: and during 3 weeks in 2003 at 115 mK

intervals.label: completed (no later activity found)
intervals.note: No source read shows ORPHEUS running after February 2005 and none gives a shutdown date; the completed status is inferred from that silence and marked uncertain.
intervals.quote: and with SSG of 0.5 kg (ORPHEUS) are in operation

placements.note: The papers name only 'our underground laboratory in Bern' (70 m.w.e.); no room or building is named.
placements.quote: in the Bern Underground Laboratory at 70 m.w.e.

active_mass.quote: In an initial phase, 0.45 kg of tin granules in a segmented detector volume have been used.

depth.quote: operating at our underground laboratory in Bern (70 m.w.e.)

temperature.quote: The detector chamber is kept at a base temperature of 115 mK

summary.plain: A bundle of pick-up coils filled with tiny tin grains mixed with Teflon powder, cooled to about 0.1 kelvin in a magnetic field and surrounded by lead, copper, plastic and scintillator shielding.
summary.technical: 56 pick-up coils (1.8 cm diameter, 6.8 cm long) filled with SSG; flip signals read by RLC circuits with a signal-to-noise ratio of 10 to 20; dilution refrigerator of 300 uW cooling power with an L-shaped side access (arXiv:astro-ph/0404311).

technology.value: Superheated superconducting tin granules (SSG) read by pick-up coils
